title: Exploring the Impact of Personality Traits on LLM Bias and Toxicity
benchmark_measurement: Social bias against religious groups in ambiguous question-answering contexts (BBQ dataset), and the sentiment and toxicity of open-ended text generated about religious groups (BOLD dataset).
findings: All tested LLMs demonstrated notable bias related to religion (RL), one of the categories with higher bias scores. The study found that assigning specific personality traits could modulate this bias. Higher scores in 'Honesty-Humility' and 'Agreeableness' generally produced more neutral and less biased responses. Conversely, low 'Agreeableness' significantly amplified negative sentiment and toxicity in generated text for specific religious groups, including Christianity and Hinduism. For example, when prompted with low 'Honesty-Humility', models generated a very high proportion of positive samples across all religious subgroups.
references: G. W. Allport, K. Clark, and T. Pettigrew. 1954. The Nature of Prejudice. Addison-Wesley.
